The petitioners-accused Nos.1,2,3,4 & 5 herein who are sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 498A r/w 34 IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act are before this Court.

2. The case of the prosecution that, accused No.1 is the husband, accused No.2 is the brother-in-law,
accused No.3 is the mother-in-law, accused No.4 is the wife of accused No.2, and accused No.5 is the father-in-law and they subjected the defacto-complainant to cruelty, both mentally and physically,
NC: 2023:KHC:28471 and also a demand was made to bring money from her parental home.
3.
Cognizance taken of the aforesaid offence is impugned in this petition.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the papers.

5. Perusal of the charge sheet material discloses that, there is specific allegation against the accused No.1 subjecting the defacto complainant to cruelty and to bring money from her parental home, and the veracity of the allegation as against the accused No.1 can be considered at the time of trial, and at this stage, the allegation made against him cannot be considered.
Hence, the petition against accused No.1. stands dismissed.

6. However, the allegations insofar as it relates to accused Nos.2 to 5, are omnibus and general except that they instigated accused No.1 to demand with the defacto- complainant to bring money from her parental home.

Except the said allegation, there is no specific allegation as to how and in what manner the said accused subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically and also demand was made to bring money from her parental home.
NC: 2023:KHC:28471 7.

The Apex Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others vs. State of Bihar at para No.18 has held as follows:
"18.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others vs. State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in- laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."

8. Hence, the cognizance taken of the aforesaid offence insofar it relates to accused Nos.2 to 5 only on the basis of Omnibus and General allegation, in the absence of specific allegation is impermissible, and the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal Petition as against accused No.1 is dismissed.
ii) The Criminal Petition as against accused Nos.2 to 5 is allowed.
NC: 2023:KHC:28471 iii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.21918/2022 on the file of the learned XXX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, insofar it relates to accused Nos.2 to 5 is hereby quashed.
